mechanism_chain.process: Architectural environment presents multi-sensory stimulus array: visual appearance (colour, texture, luminance), acoustic character (reverberation, sound absorption, ambient spectrum), haptic properties (surface temperature, roughness, compliance), olfactory signature (material VOCs, moisture, age)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Parallel sensory processing in modality-specific cortices

mechanism_chain.process: Brain evaluates crossmodal congruency: do the sensory channels align along expected correspondence dimensions? Warm visual appearance + warm haptic feel + soft acoustic absorption + wood scent = CONGRUENT. Warm visual appearance + cold haptic feel + hard reverberation + chemical scent = INCONGRUENT.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Superior temporal sulcus; inferior frontal gyrus — congruency evaluation

mechanism_chain.process: Congruent multi-sensory arrays produce processing fluency: the brain processes the environment with less computational effort, generating a positive metacognitive signal (things 'feel right'). Incongruent arrays produce disfluency: increased processing effort, negative metacognitive signal (things 'feel wrong').
mechanism_chain.substrate: Prefrontal fluency monitoring → affect generation via somatic marker pathway

mechanism_chain.process: Fluency/disfluency signal modulates environmental affect: congruent environments are rated as more pleasant, more coherent, more trustworthy. Incongruent environments produce unease, suspicion, reduced dwelling time.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Orbitofrontal cortex valuation; anterior insula interoceptive integration

congruency_affect_boost.interpretation: Crossmodally congruent environments are rated ~0.30–0.50 standard deviations more pleasant than incongruent environments, controlling for individual channel quality.

key_correspondence_dimensions.warm_cool: Visual warmth (warm colours, wood textures) ↔ haptic warmth (low λ surfaces) ↔ acoustic warmth (low reverberation, absorptive surfaces) ↔ olfactory warmth (wood, vanilla, cinnamon VOCs)
key_correspondence_dimensions.rough_smooth: Visual roughness (textured surfaces) ↔ haptic roughness (high Ra) ↔ acoustic roughness (diffuse, scattered sound) ↔ olfactory 'roughness' (earthy, mineral scents)
key_correspondence_dimensions.bright_dark: Visual brightness ↔ high-pitched ambient sounds ↔ smooth haptic surfaces ↔ 'bright' scents (citrus, mint)

incongruency_detection_threshold.interpretation: A single misaligned correspondence dimension (e.g., warm visuals + cold haptics) produces detectable disfluency. Two or more misaligned dimensions produce strong negative affect.

material_authenticity_as_congruency.interpretation: Authentic materials produce inherently congruent multi-sensory signals (real wood looks, feels, and smells like wood). Simulated materials (wood-print laminate) produce inherent incongruency (looks like wood, feels like plastic). This is the primary architectural source of crossmodal incongruency.

expertise.effect: Architects, designers, and aesthetically trained individuals are MORE sensitive to crossmodal incongruency (lower detection threshold, stronger negative affect from misalignment).

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Crossmodal incongruency is a form of prediction error that the body budget must process. Under allostatic deficit, the processing cost of incongruency is experienced more negatively (lower tolerance for things that 'feel wrong'). Congruent environments are easier on the body budget because they require less processing effort.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Crossmodal congruency contributes to environmental predictability, which supports perceived control. When sensory channels agree (what you see is what you get when you touch), the environment is predictable. When they disagree (wood-print laminate), the environment is deceptive, undermining trust and control.

cross_template_references: MATERIAL_IDENTITY_INTEGRATION_001 — congruency is a prerequisite for optimal MLE integration
CROSSMODAL_CONGRUENCE_001 — spatial coherence is a specific case of congruency (spatial alignment of multi-sensory signals)
NATURAL_MATERIAL_CONVERGENCE_001 — natural materials are inherently congruent; this is part of their stress reduction advantage
name: Crossmodal Congruency → Processing Fluency → Affect

correspondence_alignment_score.interpretation: Number of correspondence dimensions aligned across channels / total number of dimensions. Score of 1.0 = perfect congruency across all channels.

material_simulation_penalty.interpretation: Each simulated material (laminate pretending to be wood, vinyl pretending to be stone) introduces a crossmodal incongruency that reduces overall environmental pleasantness.
